text:
jamie: quick sync on the probe-hysteresis experiment i pushed to staging. goal: reduce probe thrash and unintended KV churn while keeping microburst latency low.

nina: tl;dr results?

jamie: overall fewer probe opens (~30% drop) and lower KV allocation rate. p50 for tiny requests down a bit, p99 slightly up on 3 out of 8 hosts where probe cooldown was too short.

omar: curious what you changed vs the first probe pass.

jamie: two main changes: (1) per-tenant probe cooldown that grows with consecutive probe failures (hysteresis), (2) a cooldown jitter to avoid synchronized reopen storms.

chen: how does the cooldown interact with the probe token bucket? do tokens refill during cooldown?

jamie: tokens are frozen during cooldown. refill resumes after cooldown expires. this prevents fast retry loops where token refill + immediate probe re-open cause repeated warmups.

nina: can you paste the pseudo-config you tried?

jamie: sure:

```
probe.enabled = true
probe.window_ms = 9
probe.tokens_per_tenant = 4
probe.token_refill_ms = 2000
probe.cooldown.base_ms = 50
probe.cooldown.multiplier = 2.5
probe.cooldown.max_ms = 2000
probe.cooldown.jitter_pct = 0.15
probe.kv_warmup_tag = "probe_no_warmup"
```

omar: multiplier 2.5 is aggressive; after 3 failures cooldown becomes ~312ms, then 780ms, etc. that's probably why p99 spiked on some hosts.

jamie: right. we observed one noisy tenant causing quick escalation. i added a safety cap: global probe_concurrency_limit = 200 across pool; when hit, all probes short-circuit to immediate backpressure.

chen: do we track a per-tenant probe_failure_count metric? that'll help spot gaming.

jamie: added metrics: probe.open_count, probe.fail_count, probe.cooldown_ms (per-tenant histogram), probe_kv_skips. also surfaced tenant_probe_ratio for heatmap.

deploy-bot: deploy: branch "probe-hysteresis-v1" rolled to staging at 2026-03-24T14:08:00Z. watch /eng-runtime/telemetry/probe_hysteresis.

nina: can we get traces for a sample of escalations? need to see where p99 increases come from (packing vs queueing).

jamie: yes — i set trace sampling: probe_path = 2%, normal_path = 0.2%, escalation_path = 10% for the first hour post-deploy.

omar: another angle: if probes skip KV warmup, successful probes will still need to warm KV when they transition to normal admission. that might cause a delayed warmup spike. how do we avoid that?

jamie: two mitigations: (A) when a probe wins and is about to be promoted, we perform a lightweight KV prefetch (non-blocking) rather than full allocation, then promote on first real request. (B) stagger promotion windows by tenant hash to smooth warmup across the pool.

chen: do we need an admission API change? current admission call assumes immediate KV allocation. are we annotating requests or adding an admission flag?

jamie: we added an optional header: X-Probe-Mode: probe|promote|normal. runtime treats probe as no-kv, promote as prefetch-only, normal as full. that's backwards-compatible; controllers that don't set header see normal flow.

nina: i worry about observability gaps. we must ensure downstream telemetry attributes trace spans with probe state. otherwise it's impossible to reason about effects.

jamie: agreed — added span tag probe.mode and probe.cooldown_ms. also emitting log event when a tenant enters cooldown for > 100ms.

omar: operational playbook? what should oncall do if they see pool-wide p99 rise after enabling probes?

chen: proposal: first flip feature flag off globally (fast rollback), if not possible trigger emergency short-circuit (configurable) that makes probes no-op, then hunt tenant by tenant_probe_ratio heatmap.

qa-bot: checklist created: [ ] smoke test small/large requests [ ] heatmap sanity [ ] KV-prefetch validation [ ] trace sampling verification.

nina: next steps?

jamie: 1) tune multiplier down to 1.8 and run 24h A/B (owner: jamie)
2) add tenant-level alert for probe.cooldown_ms > 500ms for >1m (owner: chen)
3) dashboard: probe_open_rate, probe_promotion_latency, kv_prefetch_rate (owner: omar)
4) update admission API doc with X-Probe-Mode semantics (owner: nina)

omar: +1. add a small note in rollout plan about trace sampling to keep storage sane.

jamie: will post A/B link and bucketed numbers tmrw. thanks all.

nina: great work — cautious approach seems solid. :thumbsup:
